title: Asteroid calc dispatch (all backends) + main-asteroid golden battery
description:
# Asteroid calc dispatch across all three ephemeris sources + main-asteroid golden battery

## Summary
Route `Body::Chiron..Vesta` and `Body::Asteroid(n)` through the calc pipeline. Structural C truth (c-ref-asteroid.md §1.4): **the asteroid position itself ALWAYS comes from the `.se1` file, for every ephemeris source** — `ephemeris_source` only selects how Earth/Sun are computed. Golden battery for the six main asteroids against C `swe_calc`.

## Architecture decisions (made — do not re-litigate)
1. **MOSEPH + asteroid** implements C's *fresh-process* semantics (c-ref-asteroid.md §1.5): heliocentric asteroid + heliocentric Moshier Earth + all-zero `sun_bary`. C's stale-global frame-mixing quirk is NOT reproducible statelessly and is not modeled. MOSEPH goldens are generated in a fresh process that never issues SWIEPH calls (follow-up task handles those; this task is SWIEPH/JPL goldens only).
2. **Asteroid-file failures map to `Error::EphemerisNotAvailable`** (never `BeyondEphemerisLimits`) so `calc_inner`'s Swiss→Moshier fallback can never fire *for the asteroid itself* — C parity: missing/out-of-range asteroid file is a hard NOT_AVAILABLE with no retry (§1.4). Earth-file failures still surface as `BeyondEphemerisLimits` from the inner provider and DO trigger the existing Swiss→Moshier fallback — which reproduces C's `app_pos_etc_plan`-failure `goto do_asteroid` MOSEPH retry (Earth via Moshier, asteroid still from file).
3. **One file per calc call**: `asteroid_file_for` selects the file at the request jd; light-time re-evaluations reuse that same `&SwissEphFile` (C's open-file caching does exactly this — the retarded epoch never re-selects a file).

## Files
- `src/calc.rs` — `normalize_asteroid_aliases`, `AsteroidProvider`, `MoshierEarthProvider`, `calc_asteroid_sweph/jpl/moshier`.
- `src/context.rs` — alias call + Chiron/Pholus guards in `calc_inner`; `asteroid_file_for` helper; asteroid arms in `calc_body_sweph/jpl/moshier`.
- `src/sweph_file/mod.rs` — `body_file_id` asteroid arms.
- `src/constants.rs` — `CHIRON_START/CHIRON_END/PHOLUS_START/PHOLUS_END`.
- `src/phenomena.rs` — `normalize_pheno_body` delegates to the shared alias helper.
- `tests/c-gen/gen_asteroid.c`, `tests/golden/asteroid.rs`, `tests/golden/main.rs` (add `mod asteroid;`).

## Implementation steps
1. **Alias helper** in calc.rs: `pub(crate) fn normalize_asteroid_aliases(body: Body) -> Body` — `Asteroid(134340)` → `Pluto` (C does this in `swe_calc` itself, sweph.c:365, before any dispatch — §1.1 note); `Asteroid(1..=4)` → `Ceres..Vesta` (§1.1 row 2: C rewrites both ipl and ipli so 10001–10004 are bit-identical to the named constants). Call it at the TOP of `calc_inner` (context.rs:1277) so every entry point (calc, calc_ut, speed3, pctr callers, eclipse, pheno…) inherits it. Refactor `phenomena.rs::normalize_pheno_body` (line 87) to delegate — its mapping is identical; keep the fn + doc, body becomes one call.
2. **`body_file_id`** (sweph_file/mod.rs:81): add `Chiron => Some(12), Pholus => Some(13), Ceres => Some(14), Pallas => Some(15), Juno => Some(16), Vesta => Some(17)` — hex-dump-verified seas `ipl[]` scheme (c-ref-asteroid.md §6, first porting-notes bullet) — and `Asteroid(id) => Some(10000 + id.mpc_number())`. These ids are only ever looked up in asteroid files; planet files don't contain them, so the shared fn stays safe.
3. **Constants** (constants.rs): `CHIRON_START = 1967601.5`, `CHIRON_END = 3419437.5`, `PHOLUS_START = 640648.5`, `PHOLUS_END = 4390617.5` (c-ref-asteroid.md §5).
4. **Guards in `calc_inner`**, immediately after the alias call and BEFORE the ephemeris-source match (C places them in `swecalc` before everything, §1.3 — they apply to every source and must bypass the Swiss→Moshier fallback, which an early return does): `Chiron` outside `[CHIRON_START, CHIRON_END]` → `Err(Error::BeyondEphemerisLimits { jd_tt, start: CHIRON_START, end: CHIRON_END })`; same shape for `Pholus`.
5. **`asteroid_file_for`** on `Ephemeris` (context.rs): `fn asteroid_file_for(&self, body: Body, jd: f64) -> Result<(&SwissEphFile, i32), Error>`.
   - Main asteroids (Chiron..Vesta): `find_file_for_jd(&self.main_asteroid_files, sei_id, jd)` (sweph_file/mod.rs:130 — works unchanged over the seas series) → `Err(Error::EphemerisNotAvailable { body, source: self.config.ephemeris_source })` if `None`.
   - `Asteroid(n)`: linear scan `self.asteroid_files` for `planets()[0].body_id == 10000 + n`; not found → `EphemerisNotAvailable` (doc-comment: the number must be listed in `config.asteroid_numbers`). Found but jd outside that body's `tfstart..=tfend` → `EphemerisNotAvailable` too (decision 2 above).
6. **`AsteroidProvider`** in calc.rs, near `SwephProvider` (line 1387): `pub(crate) struct AsteroidProvider<'a, P: PositionProvider> { inner: &'a P, ast_file: &'a SwissEphFile, ast_id: i32 }` implementing `PositionProvider`:
   - `positions(_body, jd, need_speed)`: `let pos = self.inner.positions(Body::Sun, jd, need_speed)?` (the `Body::Sun` dummy-query populates `earth_bary`/`sun_bary`/`earth_helio` on every provider — same established pattern as `nodaps_observer`, context.rs:809). Then `let (mut ast, _) = evaluate_body(self.ast_file, self.ast_id, jd, need_speed)?` (ROTATE/ELLIPSE handled inside — asteroids use both flags, c-ref-asteroid.md §6 output-frame bullet). Then the helio→bary add, mirroring `sweph_positions`'s existing branch (calc.rs:1364-1370): if `ast_file.planet_data(ast_id).iflg & SEI_FLG_HELIO != 0` → `ast[i] += pos.sun_bary[i]` for the live components. Return `SwephPositions { planet_bary: ast, ..pos-fields }`.
   - `moon_geo`: delegate to `self.inner.moon_geo`.
   - Note the MOSEPH elegance: with `MoshierEarthProvider`'s all-zero `sun_bary` the helio→bary add is a no-op, so the asteroid stays heliocentric against a heliocentric Earth — exactly C's fresh-process MOSEPH state (decision 1).
7. **`MoshierEarthProvider`** in calc.rs: struct holding the per-call `eps_j2000: &Epsilon` (or compute internally). `positions(_body, jd, need_speed)`: `let pp = crate::moshier::backend::compute_pipeline(jd, Body::Sun, eps_j2000)?` → `SwephPositions { planet_bary: [0.0; 6], earth_bary: pp.earth_helio, earth_helio: pp.earth_helio, sun_bary: [0.0; 6] }` (mirrors `nodaps_observer`'s Moshier arm, context.rs:818-830). `moon_geo`: `crate::calc::raw_osc_moon_moshier(jd, eps_j2000)` (calc.rs:1284) — apparent_planet doesn't call it for planets, but implement it real rather than `unreachable!`.
8. **`calc_asteroid_sweph/jpl/moshier`** in calc.rs next to `calc_planet_sweph` (line 1916), same signature shape plus `ast_file: &SwissEphFile, ast_id: i32`: construct the inner provider (`SwephProvider`/`JplProvider`/`MoshierEarthProvider`), wrap in `AsteroidProvider`, call `apparent_planet(&p, jd, body, eps_j2000, flags, config, models)`. The generic pipeline (light-time, aberration, deflection, HELCTR branch, TOPOCTR via topo_offset, J2000/SIDEREAL tails) applies to asteroids with zero asteroid-specific deltas (c-ref-asteroid.md §1.6/§6).
9. **Dispatch arms** in `calc_body_sweph` (context.rs:1427), `calc_body_jpl` (1477), `calc_body_moshier` (1398): add `Body::Chiron | Body::Pholus | Body::Ceres | Body::Pallas | Body::Juno | Body::Vesta | Body::Asteroid(_) => { let (f, id) = self.asteroid_file_for(body, jd_tt)?; crate::calc::calc_asteroid_<src>(...) }`. The Moshier arm works whenever `ephe_path` was configured (task swisseph-rs/100 loads asteroid files for all sources); with no files loaded, `asteroid_file_for` returns `EphemerisNotAvailable` — C parity.
10. **`gen_asteroid.c`** (tests/c-gen, follow gen_calc_sweph.c's JSON emission + gen_pheno.c's header-comment build instructions): `swe_set_ephe_path("ephe")` — run from repo root; `<repo>/ephe` carries sepl+semo+seas+ast dirs (the C-side `../swisseph/ephe` does NOT have ast dirs — do not point there). Matrix:
    - Bodies: `SE_CHIRON(15), SE_PHOLUS(16), SE_CERES(17), SE_PALLAS(18), SE_JUNO(19), SE_VESTA(20)`.
    - Epochs: `2451545.0` (J2000), `2460310.5` (2024), `2433282.5` (1950), `2415020.5` (1900), `2305447.5` (1600 — exercises the seas_12 file-selection path; still ≥ CHIRON_START).
    - Flag combos (10): `SWIEPH`, `SWIEPH|SPEED`, `SWIEPH|SPEED|EQUATORIAL`, `SWIEPH|SPEED|XYZ`, `SWIEPH|SPEED|J2000|NONUT` (match the calc battery's j2000 shape), `SWIEPH|TRUEPOS`, `SWIEPH|NONUT`, `SWIEPH|SPEED|TOPOCTR` (with `swe_set_topo(8.55, 47.37, 500)` once at start), `SWIEPH|SPEED|HELCTR`, `JPLEPH|SPEED` (de441.eph is in ephe/).
    - = 300 cases. Emit per case: `body`, `body_name`, `jd`, `flags`, `flag_name`, `retflag`, `output[6]`. Abort (nonzero exit, stderr) on any `swe_calc` error — every case must succeed C-side.
    - NO MOSEPH cases in this generator (decision 1 — process-state hazard; they live in the follow-up coverage task).
11. **`tests/golden/asteroid.rs`**: mirror calc_sweph.rs structure. `body_from_c_id` extended for 15..=20. `Ephemeris` with `ephe_path = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("ephe")` (NOT `../swisseph/ephe`), `ephemeris_source: Swiss` (JPLEPH rows: a second Ephemeris with `Jpl` source — split cases by flag bit, same file). Assert positions eps `1e-9`, speeds eps `1e-7` (established sweph tolerances, tests/golden/calc_sweph.rs); `flags_used` bits equal to C `retflag` masked to the same comparison the calc_sweph test uses. Assert `cases.len() >= 300`. Register `mod asteroid;` in tests/golden/main.rs.

## C reference
`docs/c-ref-asteroid.md` — read it in full; load-bearing sections: §1.1 (alias/id mapping), §1.3 (guards), §1.4 (the bold structural paragraph + fallback cascade), §1.5 (MOSEPH quirk → decision 1), §6 (porting notes, incl. hex-verified seas ipl[] and output frame). `docs/c-ref-se1-file.md` § sweph() Steps 4–8 (already implemented as `evaluate_body`). `docs/c-ref-calc.md` §7 (pipeline — unchanged here).

## Golden tests
- C harness: `gen_asteroid.c` per step 10; build/run per its header comment (`cc -O2 -I../swisseph -o tests/c-gen/gen_asteroid tests/c-gen/gen_asteroid.c -L../swisseph -lswe -lm && ./tests/c-gen/gen_asteroid > tests/golden-data/asteroid.json`, run from repo root).
- Rust: `cargo test --test golden asteroid -- --nocapture`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo test --test golden asteroid -- --nocapture` passes: 300 cases, positions 1e-9 / speeds 1e-7, zero skips.
- Full `cargo test --test golden` and `cargo test` pass (no regressions — especially calc/calc_sweph/pheno).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` introduces no new warnings.

## Escape hatch
If golden failures with position errors > 1e-8 persist after two debugging attempts, STOP and report: failing (body, epoch, flag) triples, expected vs actual values, and what was tried. Suspects worth naming in the report rather than chasing: the helio→bary add ordering, `rot_back` ellipse handling for seas bodies, and the TOPOCTR/SPEED3 interaction. Escalate to Opus.
execution_record:
Implemented in 3 commits on main.

1. e0ac0e7: Core dispatch infrastructure — normalize_asteroid_aliases, body_file_id extensions, Chiron/Pholus guards, asteroid_file_for, AsteroidProvider/MoshierEarthProvider, calc_asteroid_sweph/jpl/moshier, dispatch arms in all three calc_body_* methods, normalize_pheno_body delegated.

2. fc7d685: Golden battery + helio→bary fix. Key surprise: seas .se1 files do NOT set SEI_FLG_HELIO on asteroid entries — C's helio→bary conversion is guarded on `ipl >= SEI_ANYBODY` (slot-index check), not the per-planet flag byte. First attempt gated the add on SEI_FLG_HELIO and got ~0.03° errors. Fixed to unconditionally add sun_bary; MoshierEarthProvider's all-zero sun_bary makes the add a no-op under MOSEPH.

3. 771a403: Codebase map update.

JPLEPH tolerance: C returns SWIEPH in retflag for JPLEPH+asteroid (the asteroid file is always .se1). JPLEPH position tolerance widened to 2e-6 for the JPL-vs-SWIEPH Earth/Sun source difference (worst ~1.2e-6 at epoch 1600).

messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (3 findings):

1. [high] evaluate_body inside AsteroidProvider can return BeyondEphemerisLimits at retarded epochs, which calc_inner catches and triggers Swiss→Moshier fallback — violating the contract that asteroid-file failures should be EphemerisNotAvailable. Practically impractical (light-time ~0.01 days vs file spans of centuries), but a contract gap.

2. [medium] Golden test silently skips all JPL cases if eph_jpl construction fails — zero-skips acceptance criterion isn't enforced.

3. [medium] Main asteroid file parse errors swallowed by unwrap_or_default in Ephemeris::new — OUT OF SCOPE, pre-existing from task 100.
